title: Invoice Balance Dispute
question_for_arbitration: We, Valencia Industrial Supply, Inc., seek payment of the remaining balance on Invoice VP-INV-260210 arising from the February 2026 order placed by Monterrey Fleet Solutions, LLC. The invoice was originally $29,500. Monterrey paid $8,000, and we issued a $1,500 credit, leaving a current account balance of $20,000 before any further adjustments determined through this arbitration. The dispute concerns the applicable product pricing, a four-filter quantity discrepancy, the $500 expedited delivery/handling charge, and the $1,875 inventory-management service charge.
other_relief: No non-monetary relief is requested. Valencia also requests any interest properly available under Supply & Services Agreement §8.5 on amounts determined to be properly due and unpaid after the applicable payment date.
arbitration_clause: This arbitration shall be administered by DecisionLayer.AI under its Foundational + Strict Contractual Ruleset, subject to the law of New York and the Federal Arbitration Act. The arbitration will be held online through DecisionLayer.ai. Both parties agree to resolve any claims relating to or arising out of these Terms or the Services through final and binding individual arbitration by a single arbitrator. Class arbitrations, class actions, private attorney general actions, and consolidation with other arbitrations are not allowed. The arbitrator may award relief only individually and only to the extent necessary to redress individual claims. The DecisionLayer rules will govern payment of all arbitration fees. Valencia Industrial Supply will not seek its attorneys' fees and costs in arbitration unless the arbitrator determines that the claim is frivolous or brought for an improper purpose.
governing_contract:
VALENCIA INDUSTRIAL SUPPLY, INC.
MONTERREY FLEET SOLUTIONS, LLC
SUPPLY & SERVICES AGREEMENT
Effective Date: January 15, 2026

1. This Supply & Services Agreement (“Agreement”) is entered into between Valencia Industrial Supply, Inc., a California corporation with its principal place of business in Fresno, California (“Supplier”), and Monterrey Fleet Solutions, LLC, a Nevada limited liability company with its principal place of business in Henderson, Nevada (“Customer”).
Supplier provides industrial maintenance parts, replacement components, and related inventory-management services to commercial customers. Customer operates commercial fleet-maintenance facilities and purchases maintenance parts and related services from Supplier.
The parties intend this Agreement to establish the terms governing Customer’s purchase of products and related inventory-management services from Supplier, including ordering, pricing, delivery, returns, invoicing, payment, credits, and resolution of disputes concerning amounts charged under this Agreement.

2. ORDERS AND PURCHASE ORDERS
2.1 Purchase Orders. Customer may order Products or Services by submitting a written purchase order to Supplier. Each purchase order (“Purchase Order”) should identify, as applicable, the Products or Services requested, quantities, applicable prices, requested delivery dates, delivery location, and any other information reasonably necessary to fulfill the order.
2.2 Acceptance of Orders. A Purchase Order becomes binding when Supplier accepts it in writing, confirms the order, begins performance, or ships Products in response to the Purchase Order.
2.3 Relationship to this Agreement. Each accepted Purchase Order is subject to this Agreement. If a Purchase Order contains a term that conflicts with this Agreement, this Agreement controls unless the Purchase Order expressly identifies the conflicting provision of this Agreement and states that the parties intend to modify that provision for that particular order.
2.4 Changes to Orders. Any change to the Products, quantities, prices, delivery requirements, or Services specified in an accepted Purchase Order must be agreed to by both parties in writing.
2.5 Records. Each party will maintain commercially reasonable records relating to accepted Purchase Orders, including order confirmations, delivery records, receiving records, and written changes or communications concerning the order.


3. PRICING
3.1 Agreed Prices. The prices for Products and Services will be the prices stated in the applicable accepted Purchase Order, quotation, or pricing schedule agreed to by the parties in writing.
3.2 Purchase Order Pricing. Unless the parties expressly agree otherwise in writing, the unit prices stated in an accepted Purchase Order will apply to the Products covered by that Purchase Order. Supplier may not increase the price for Products after acceptance of a Purchase Order without Customer’s written agreement.
3.3 Pricing Adjustments. Any adjustment to an agreed price must be communicated in writing and accepted by both parties before the adjusted price applies. An adjustment may apply only to the Products, Services, quantities, or orders specifically identified in the written agreement.
3.4 Taxes and Shipping. Unless otherwise stated in the applicable Purchase Order, prices exclude applicable sales or similar transaction taxes and reasonable shipping or delivery charges. Taxes and shipping charges must be separately identified on the applicable invoice.
3.5 No Implied Charges. Supplier may not charge Customer for Products, Services, fees, or other amounts that are not authorized by this Agreement, an accepted Purchase Order, or a subsequent written agreement between the parties.

4. DELIVERY AND ACCEPTANCE
4.1 Delivery. Supplier will deliver Products to the delivery location and by the requested delivery date stated in the applicable accepted Purchase Order, subject to reasonable delays outside Supplier’s control.
4.2 Delivery Records. Supplier may provide packing slips, shipment records, delivery confirmations, or similar records identifying the Products and quantities shipped. Customer will maintain commercially reasonable receiving records for Products delivered to its facilities.
4.3 Inspection. Customer will reasonably inspect Products after delivery. Customer must notify Supplier in writing of any apparent shortage, incorrect quantity, visible damage, or other delivery discrepancy within 10 business days after delivery.
4.4 Latent Defects. A defect that could not reasonably have been discovered through ordinary inspection at delivery may be reported within a reasonable period after Customer discovers, or reasonably should have discovered, the defect.
4.5 Acceptance. Products will be deemed accepted as to quantity and apparent condition if Customer does not timely notify Supplier of a discrepancy under Section 4.3. Acceptance does not waive a claim concerning a latent defect or a discrepancy that could not reasonably have been discovered through ordinary inspection.
4.6 Disputed Delivery Records. If the parties disagree about the quantity or condition of Products delivered, the parties will use their delivery, receiving, return, and other contemporaneous business records to determine the quantity and condition of Products properly chargeable to Customer.

5. RETURNS AND CREDITS
5.1 Eligible Returns. Customer may request a return of Products that are damaged on delivery, incorrectly supplied, or otherwise eligible for return under an applicable Purchase Order. Customer must provide Supplier with reasonable details identifying the Products and the reason for the requested return.
5.2 Return Authorization. Except where Supplier has confirmed in writing that authorization is not required, Customer will obtain Supplier’s written return authorization before shipping Products back to Supplier. Supplier may reasonably request photographs, receiving records, shipment information, or other documentation concerning the claimed discrepancy.
5.3 Credit for Returned Products. If Supplier confirms that returned Products qualify for a credit, Supplier will issue a credit for the applicable amount of the Products properly returned and accepted for credit. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, the credit will be applied against Customer’s account and may be applied to the invoice or invoices identified by Supplier.
5.4 Damaged or Missing Products. Where the parties agree, or the available business records establish, that Products were damaged before acceptance or were not delivered in the invoiced quantity, Supplier will issue an appropriate credit or other adjustment for the affected Products.
5.5 Timing of Credit. Supplier will use commercially reasonable efforts to process an approved credit within 15 business days after receiving the information reasonably necessary to verify the return, damage, shortage, or other qualifying adjustment.
5.6 Disputed Credits. If the parties disagree about the amount of a credit, Customer must identify the specific Products and amount disputed. The parties will use their contemporaneous Purchase Orders, delivery records, receiving records, return records, correspondence, and credit records to determine the appropriate adjustment.
5.7 No Automatic Credit. A Customer request for a return or credit does not by itself establish that a credit is owed. Eligibility and the amount of any credit will be determined under this Agreement, the applicable Purchase Order, and the parties’ supporting business records.

6. INVENTORY MANAGEMENT SERVICES
6.1 Services. If identified in an accepted Purchase Order or otherwise agreed in writing, Supplier may provide inventory-management services for Customer, including inventory monitoring, replenishment recommendations, stock counts, inventory reporting, and related administrative support.
6.2 Service Charges. Supplier may charge Customer for inventory-management services only where the applicable Purchase Order, pricing schedule, or other written agreement identifies the applicable service, rate, or recurring charge.
6.3 Performance Records. Supplier will maintain commercially reasonable records showing the inventory-management services performed, including applicable service dates, reports, inventory records, or other business records reasonably sufficient to identify the services provided.
6.4 Customer Cooperation. Customer will provide Supplier with reasonable access to information, inventory records, personnel, or facilities necessary to perform agreed inventory-management services. Delays or limitations caused by Customer may affect the timing or scope of the services.
6.5 Service Disputes. Customer must notify Supplier in writing of any material dispute concerning an inventory-management service charge and identify the specific service or period disputed. The parties will use the applicable Purchase Order, service records, inventory reports, correspondence, and other contemporaneous business records to determine whether the charge was authorized and whether the corresponding service was performed.
6.6 No Unidentified Service Charges. Supplier may not add an inventory-management service charge to an invoice unless the charge is authorized under Section 6.2.


7. INVOICING
7.1 Invoices. Supplier may issue invoices for Products and Services provided under accepted Purchase Orders. Each invoice will identify, as applicable, the relevant Purchase Order, Products or Services billed, quantities, applicable prices, credits or adjustments, taxes, shipping or other authorized charges, and the total amount due.
7.2 Invoice Delivery. Supplier may deliver invoices electronically, including through a third-party billing or payment platform designated by Supplier. Customer agrees that an electronic invoice delivered through such a platform constitutes delivery of the invoice for purposes of this Agreement.
7.3 Calculation of Charges. Invoice amounts must be calculated using the prices and charges authorized under this Agreement, the applicable accepted Purchase Order, and any subsequent written modification agreed by the parties.
7.4 Credits and Adjustments. Supplier will identify material credits or adjustments applicable to an invoice on the invoice itself or on a related credit memo or account statement. A credit or adjustment may be applied against the invoice to which it relates or, where the parties agree, against another outstanding amount owed by Customer.
7.5 Invoice Records. Each party will maintain commercially reasonable records relating to invoices, including invoices received or issued, payment records, credit records, and written communications concerning disputed charges.
7.6 Electronic Billing Records. Where invoices or payments are processed through a third-party billing or payment platform, the parties may use records generated by that platform, including invoice histories, payment confirmations, account statements, credit records, and transaction histories, as business records concerning the transaction.
7.7 No Waiver by Invoicing Error. An error in an invoice does not by itself waive Supplier’s right to collect an amount that is otherwise properly owed under this Agreement. The parties will correct confirmed billing errors through an appropriate revised invoice, credit, debit, or other account adjustment.

8. PAYMENT
8.1 Payment Due Date. Customer will pay each undisputed invoice within 30 calendar days after the date of the invoice, unless a different payment period is stated in the applicable Purchase Order.
8.2 Payment of Undisputed Amounts. Customer will timely pay amounts that it does not dispute. A good-faith dispute concerning part of an invoice does not excuse Customer from paying the undisputed portion of that invoice.
8.3 Partial Payments. A payment that is less than the total invoiced amount will be applied to the invoice in accordance with the parties’ written agreement or, absent such agreement, first to amounts that are not subject to a good-faith dispute and then to the remaining balance.
8.4 Payment Records. Payments made through a third-party billing or payment platform may be evidenced by the platform’s payment confirmation, transaction record, account statement, or other electronic record identifying the amount, date, payer, payee, and applicable invoice.
8.5 Late Payment. Amounts that are properly due and remain unpaid after the applicable due date may accrue interest at the lesser of 1% per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, beginning on the date the amount became overdue.
8.6 No Waiver Through Partial Payment. Acceptance of a partial payment does not, by itself, constitute agreement concerning the amount of any remaining disputed balance.

9. INVOICE DISPUTES
9.1 Notice of Dispute. If Customer disputes any portion of an invoice, Customer must provide Supplier with written notice within 10 business days after receiving the invoice. The notice must identify the specific invoice, the disputed charge or charges, and, to the extent reasonably known, the basis and amount of the dispute.
9.2 Undisputed Amounts. Customer will timely pay all portions of an invoice that are not subject to a good-faith dispute. Customer may withhold only the amount reasonably related to the disputed charges while the dispute is being resolved.
9.3 Review and Supporting Records. Following receipt of a timely dispute notice, the parties will reasonably cooperate to review the records relevant to the disputed charges, which may include Purchase Orders, delivery and receiving records, return records, service records, invoices, credit memos, payment records, and written communications.
9.4 Supplier Response. Supplier will review a properly submitted dispute and provide a written response within 10 business days, including any correction, credit, supporting explanation, or request for additional information that Supplier reasonably considers necessary to resolve the dispute.
9.5 Good-Faith Resolution. The parties will attempt in good faith to resolve a properly submitted invoice dispute through their designated business representatives before commencing arbitration concerning that dispute.
9.6 Effect of Failure to Dispute. Failure to timely dispute an invoice will constitute evidence that the invoice was accepted as to the charges that Customer reasonably could have identified through ordinary review, but will not prevent Customer from raising a claim based on a latent defect, fraud, unauthorized charge not reasonably discoverable from the invoice, or another matter that could not reasonably have been identified within the dispute period.
9.7 No Waiver of Substantive Rights. Participation in the invoice-dispute process, including the payment of an undisputed amount or issuance of a partial credit, does not by itself waive either party’s substantive rights concerning the disputed amount.


10. CREDITS AND ACCOUNT ADJUSTMENTS
10.1 Issued Credits. Any credit issued by Supplier will identify, to the extent reasonably practicable, the invoice, Products, Services, or other transaction to which the credit relates and the amount of the credit.
10.2 Application of Credits. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, an issued credit will be applied against the invoice or account balance identified in the applicable credit record.
10.3 Additional Adjustments. If Customer believes that an additional credit or adjustment is required, Customer must identify the specific charge or transaction giving rise to the requested adjustment and provide reasonably available supporting records.
10.4 Review of Adjustments. Supplier will reasonably review a requested adjustment and may issue an additional credit, revise the applicable invoice, or explain in writing why the requested adjustment is not supported by the available records.
10.5 Disputed Credit Amounts. An issued credit establishes the amount Supplier has agreed to credit at that time, but does not by itself prevent Customer from disputing whether an additional adjustment is required under this Agreement.
10.6 Account Reconciliation. Where the parties disagree about the balance of an account, they will use the applicable invoices, Purchase Orders, payment records, credit records, returns, delivery records, service records, and other contemporaneous business records to prepare and compare their respective reconciliations.


11. CURE AND CORRECTION
11.1 Notice of Performance Issue. If Customer believes that Supplier has failed to provide Products or Services in accordance with this Agreement or an applicable Purchase Order, Customer will provide Supplier with reasonably specific written notice describing the issue and, where practicable, the affected Products, Services, or charges.
11.2 Opportunity to Cure. Where a failure is reasonably capable of correction, Supplier will have a reasonable opportunity to investigate and cure the issue after receiving notice. The parties will cooperate in good faith to determine an appropriate corrective action.
11.3 Commercially Reasonable Cure. Depending on the circumstances, a cure may include replacement of Products, completion or correction of Services, issuance of a credit, correction of an invoice, refund of an overpayment, or another commercially reasonable adjustment agreed by the parties.
11.4 No Automatic Waiver. Customer's acceptance of a proposed cure does not waive a separate claim concerning an amount or issue that remains unresolved. Likewise, Supplier's attempt to cure or issue a credit does not constitute an admission that all amounts disputed by Customer were improperly charged.
11.5 Records of Cure. The parties will maintain reasonably available records of material corrective actions, including replacement records, service records, credit memos, revised invoices, and written communications concerning the resolution of a reported issue.


12. DEFAULT AND NONPAYMENT
12.1 Payment Default. Customer will be in payment default if an amount properly due and payable under this Agreement remains unpaid after the applicable payment due date, subject to any good-faith dispute properly raised under Section 9.
12.2 Disputed Amounts. An amount that Customer has withheld in accordance with Section 9 will not constitute a payment default solely because it remains unpaid while the parties are addressing the underlying dispute.
12.3 Notice of Default. Before pursuing remedies based on nonpayment, Supplier will provide Customer with written notice identifying the unpaid amount and giving Customer at least 10 calendar days to pay the amount or explain the basis for any continuing dispute.
12.4 Continuing Dispute. If Customer maintains a good-faith dispute concerning the amount identified in a default notice, the parties will continue to use the dispute-resolution process under this Agreement for the disputed amount.
12.5 Remedies for Unpaid Amounts. Subject to this Agreement, Supplier may pursue recovery of amounts determined to be properly due and payable, together with any applicable interest and other remedies expressly permitted by this Agreement or applicable law.
12.6 No Default Based Solely on Disputed Balance. A disagreement concerning the proper calculation of an invoice does not, by itself, establish that either party has breached this Agreement. The parties' respective rights will depend on the applicable contractual provisions and the evidence concerning the disputed charges.


13. LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
13.1 Exclusion of Certain Damages. Except for amounts expressly owed for Products or Services, neither party will be liable to the other for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, exemplary, or punitive damages arising out of or relating to this Agreement, whether based in contract, tort, or otherwise.
13.2 Liability Cap. Except for the exclusions in Section 13.3, each party’s aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the total amounts paid or payable by Customer to Supplier under the applicable Purchase Orders during the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
13.3 Exceptions. The limitations in this Section do not apply to:
(a) Customer’s obligation to pay amounts properly due for Products or Services;
(b) either party’s fraud, willful misconduct, or intentional misrepresentation;
(c) either party’s breach of its confidentiality obligations, if any; or
(d) liabilities that cannot legally be limited or excluded.
13.4 Invoice Dispute Unaffected. Nothing in this Section limits either party’s right to seek or defend against recovery of amounts properly due under an invoice or to obtain a credit, adjustment, refund, or other remedy expressly provided under this Agreement.


14. DISPUTE RESOLUTION AND ARBITRATION
Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this agreement, including the interpretation, formation, breach, termination, validity, arbitrability or enforceability thereof, shall be settled by binding arbitration administered by Decision Science Research Corporation (“DecisionLayer”) in accordance with its rules then in effect at https://www.decisionlayer.ai/rules (the “Rules”). The substantive rights and obligations of the parties shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York. The Federal Arbitration Act, 9 U.S.C. §§ 1–16 (“FAA”), shall govern this arbitration provision, its interpretation and enforcement, all questions of arbitrability, and the arbitration proceedings. The FAA shall control over any conflicting provision of law. EACH PARTY CONSENTS TO RECEIVE SERVICE OF PROCESS COMMENCING AN ARBITRATION VIA THE DECISIONLAYER WEBSITE (IF IT HAS AN ACCOUNT), BY EMAIL, BY REGISTERED OR CERTIFIED MAIL, OR IN ACCORDANCE WITH APPLICABLE LAWS. EACH PARTY HERETO WAIVES ANY OBJECTION TO SERVICE BY THESE MEANS.

15. GOVERNING LAW AND MISCELLANEOUS
15.1 Governing Law. Except to the extent otherwise provided in Section 14 concerning arbitration, the substantive rights and obligations of the parties under this Agreement will be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles.
15.2 Entire Agreement. This Agreement, together with its accepted Purchase Orders, written pricing schedules, and written amendments, constitutes the entire agreement between the parties concerning its subject matter and supersedes prior or contemporaneous agreements, proposals, and understandings concerning that subject matter.
15.3 Amendments. An amendment to this Agreement must be in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both parties. An amendment to a particular Purchase Order may be made in accordance with Section 2.4.
15.4 No Waiver. A party's failure to enforce any provision of this Agreement on one occasion will not constitute a waiver of that provision or prevent enforcement of the provision on another occasion.
15.5 Severability. If any provision of this Agreement is determined to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions will remain in effect to the fullest extent permitted by law.
15.6 Assignment. Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except that either party may assign this Agreement in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of substantially all of its assets, provided that the assignee assumes the assigning party's obligations.
15.7 Independent Parties. The parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency, fiduciary relationship, or employment relationship between the parties.
15.8 Electronic Communications and Signatures. The parties may execute this Agreement and related documents electronically. Electronic signatures and electronic records will have the same effect as original signatures and records to the extent permitted by applicable law.
15.9 Counterparts. This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which will be deemed an original and all of which together constitute one agreement.

16. NOTICES AND COMMUNICATIONS
16.1 Business Communications. The parties may communicate regarding orders, deliveries, invoices, payment questions, service issues, returns, credits, and other ordinary business matters by email, through an agreed billing or payment platform, or through other electronic business systems regularly used by the parties.
16.2 Formal Notices. Notices concerning material breach, termination, or commencement of arbitration must be provided in writing by email to the designated business contact of the receiving party, by nationally recognized overnight delivery service, or by certified or registered mail to the address identified below, unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.
16.3 Invoice and Account Communications. An invoice dispute, request for a credit, payment confirmation, delivery discrepancy, return request, or other ordinary account communication may be submitted by email or through the parties' designated billing or payment platform and will be effective when received.
16.4 Receipt of Electronic Communications. An electronic communication will be considered received when transmitted to the designated email address or made available through the designated billing or payment platform, provided the sender does not receive a notice that the communication was undeliverable.
